correctness.rationale: A four-term tuple with three-term prefix (2,3,7) is optimized uniquely by the least last denominator allowed by the strict real bound. Every other prefix is below beta=41/42 by classical length-three Sylvester optimality. The inequality x_(j+1)<(4-j)/(beta-s_j) bounds all potentially competitive prefixes exactly; its seven-group finite table follows by rational comparisons and yields the unique largest competitor 599/600. Exact arithmetic recreates 21 prefixes and separately 103 qualifying non-special quadruples; a single counterexample (2,3,8,25) proves sharpness on (599/600,629/630]. Real endpoints are treated with the strict inequality; no finite experiments are extrapolated.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 5 is not a uniform result for all real theta in the open sharp interval; the two-term and eventual-length results do not dominate fixed four-term exact thresholds. Neither delivers the 599/600 competing family.

value.rationale: Nathanson explicitly asks for counterexamples and behavior of best/greedy Egyptian underapproximations when length n>=3. The theorem supplies the sharp first full stability interval for n=4 together with a whole adjacent failure interval and the exact extremal obstruction rather than a single arbitrarily selected counterexample; the prefix boundary is structurally motivated by the Sylvester best length-three approximant. It is a natural complete local phase classification, not merely a reparameterized known n=2 theorem.
